episodes.182593: Evening rain and storms caused flash flooding over the southern part of the Hermits Peak Calf Canyon burn scar at San Ignacio.
episodes.182805: Two episodes of severe weather were observed over this period. The first, on August 18, was related to a ridge breakdown by a strong shortwave. Dry low and mid levels resulted in deep inverted-V profiles, which were conducive to strong wind gusts. ||The second episode of severe caliber gusts occurred on August 22nd. Moist southwesterly flow aloft, along with embedded shortwaves resulted in the developments of showers and thunderstorms across Central and Southwest Montana August 22nd. The area just experienced the remnants of Hurricane Hilary, which resulted in relatively moist lower levels, which in turn helped produce ample instability for severe thunderstorms.
episodes.182942: Scattered thunderstorms ahead of the remnants of tropical storm Harold resulted in localized severe winds.
episodes.182943: Thunderstorms associated with the remnants of tropical storm Harold resulted in a severe wind gust along the Rio Grande Valley.
episodes.182968: An isolated thunderstorm resulted in severe damaging wind gusts in McPherson County during the evening. This storm caused damage to many tree limbs.
episodes.183375: The remnants of Hurricane Hilary brought deep atmospheric moisture into the Northern Rockies. A closed upper-level low pressure system provided sufficient lift for thunderstorms, with wind shear profiles favorable for organized convection.
episodes.183882: A strong ridge over the central United States and a trough draped across the West Coast put Arizona in a position to receive a moist southerly wind flow. The 12Z sounding from|measured 0.86 inches of Precipitable Water which was slightly above average for late August...adequate monsoonal moisture to fuel storms.
episodes.183935: Hurricane Hilary moved up the Baja peninsula and dissipated in our region as an extratropical cyclone, bringing heavy rain and periods of gusty winds.
episodes.184472: A couple of thunderstorms produced some isolated severe wind gusts.
episodes.184570: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved northwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. Wind damage took place in Whetstone and also at Saguaro National Park West where hundreds of saguaros were downed or damaged. Large hail occurred in south and central Tucson, damaging an elementary school. Moderate rain from a subsequent thunderstorm leaked into the building, causing ceiling tile damage.
episodes.184732: Isolated thunderstorms moved northwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. One storm produced severe wind gusts and minor damage in Tucson.
episodes.184826: Strong southeasterly flow aloft promoted moisture advection (PWATs 1.5-1.7) into south-central Arizona along with the needed steering flow to allow thunderstorms across southeast Arizona to progress towards the Phoenix area. Effective bulk wind shear values around 35-40 knots allowed for the development of organized thunderstorms, becoming strong to severe across central and southeast Arizona. MLCAPE during this event was around 500-1,000 J/kg while DCAPE around 1,000 J/kg promoted damaging winds. During the early evening hours on the 21st, a severe thunderstorm produced damaging winds that knocked down multiple trees in Apache Junction. No injuries were reported.
episodes.184851: A thunderstorm passed across the Miley Memorial Airport near Big Piney and produced a 67 mph wind gust.
episodes.185006: Tropical Storm Harold moved west across south Texas on the 22nd. An area of low pressure developed over the central Gulf of Mexico on the 21st. A large area of high pressure over the central United States into the northern Gulf Coast steered the system quickly westward toward the Middle Texas coast. The low strengthened into Tropical Storm Harold by the early morning hours of the 22nd. Harold increased in strength and made landfall south of Baffin Bay as a 50 mph tropical storm during the late morning. Harold moved west-northwest and weakened into a tropical depression as it reached  Laredo. Beneficial rains occurred over the Coastal Bend and Brush Country with the heaviest rainfall, ranging from 5 to 7 inches, from Corpus Christi to Alice to north of Freer. Flooding occurred in Corpus Christi and Laredo. Two weak tornadoes occurred south of George West and near Orange Grove.  Tides ranged from 1 to 2 feet MHHW along the Middle Texas coast. Tidal flooding occurred around Corpus Christi and Nueces Bays with the highest tide level of 2.6 feet MHHW at Nueces Bay.
episodes.185090: Tropical storm Harold made landfall on Padre Island the morning of the 22nd. It weakened as it moved farther inland and generated thunderstorms. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.185503: High pressure building to the north of the Florida Keys resulted in increased easterly lower tropospheric winds.  Scattered showers and thunderstorms containing isolated gale force wind gusts occurred due to lower tropospheric speed convergence over the Straits of Florida.

events.narrative: A spotter reported 60 mph wind gusts near Sierra Vista.
Images and videos showed multiple large trees uprooted at the City Hall in Apache Junction. No injuries were reported.
A mobile home at Lost Dutchman RV Resort had most of its roof peeled back due to damaging winds. No injuries were reported.
Thunderstorm winds blew the corrugated metal roof off a machine shed in Whetstone.

NWS Flood survey found evidence of multiple mud/debris flow overs County Road A3A. There was also evidence of water over a bridge and culvert. Debris left behind by the waters was stuck against guard rails.
A gust to 59 mph was recorded at the Hopkins RAWS at 1833MST.
Observed by a personal weather station.
Thunderstorm winds downed 400 saguaro cacti and damaged 800 others at Saguaro National Park West.

events.narrative: An east northeast wind gust of 34 knots was measured at the navigational light at Sombrero Key.
A wind gust of 58 mph was recorded just east of Chico.
A wind gust of 59 mph was recorded just northwest of the Billings Airport.

events.narrative: A wind gust of 38 knots was measured at the navigational light at Sand Key.
The ASOS at the Boise airport measured 0.73 inches of rain. The mesonet station GW0891 one mile south of Boise measured 0.81 inches of rain.
The northwest loop exit from Interstate 37 to Highway 286 flooded.

An EF-0 tornado with 85 mph winds touched down just east of Highway 281 on County Road 151 and moved southwest along the county road. The tornado snapped large branches and split a few trees. The tornado lifted just west of Highway 281.
Flooding of streets occurred on 14th Street between Ailsie and Caesar Avenues in Kingsville.
An EF-0 tornado with 75 mph winds touched down 3 miles north of Orange Grove. The tornado moved west across Farm to Market Road 738. The tornado snapped a few branches 3 to 4 inches in diameter.
A thunderstorm from the remnants of Tropical Storm Harold produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph that damaged a roof in Seguin.

A thunderstorm generated by the remnants of Tropical Storm Harold produced wind gusts estimated at 60 mph that knocked down a six diameter Pecan tree branch at the Comal County Courthouse in New Braunfels.
Spotter reported thunderstorm wind gusts resulting in 3 large pine trees knocked down, small branches breaking, and one large branch breaking.
A vehicle drove into a flooded low water crossing 5 miles north northeast of Lake Alice. The local fire department had to perform a high water rescue.
The intersection of Highway 83/Interstate 35 and Mines Road was closed due to flood waters.
Heavy rainfall flooded several intersection from the north northeast to the south southeast parts of Laredo. Highway 83 was flooded at the intersections of Market Street and Chihuahua Street.
Flooding occurred on Highway 83 at Sierra Vista Boulevard on the extreme south side of Laredo.

Between 1 to 2.5 inches of rain fell in around two hours just east and northeast of the town of Tusayan and the South Entrance to The Grand Canyon National Park. This caused significant flooding of homes homes, buildings, and cars. Highway 64 into the GCNP was closed, shelter in place orders were put into place, and children were stuck in their school             because they could not safely get home.
Facebook reports of winds gusting at 60 to 70 mph. Multiple trees and limbs were reported down in town.

A wind gust of 68 mph was recorded at the Glacier Park International Airport. The thunderstorm resulted in a couple hundred customers without power in West Glacier and near Coram, according to Flathead Electric COOP. Numerous reports of downed trees were also received.
Off duty NWS employee estimated 60 mph winds and reported that multiple one to three inch diameter tree limbs were down.
A thunderstorm wind gust to 62 mph was recorded at KTUS ASOS at 1534MST.  Winds blew the roof off a gazebo near Catalina Highway.
Measured by MT Department of Transportation site Bowmans Corner.
Off duty NWS employee estimated 70 mph winds with a video shared via Twitter.
Measured via military AWOS station K1GM Golf.
Measured by site EW1931 Rudyard.

Multiple car crashes were reported on Interstate-90 near Missoula as a thunderstorm with strong winds and heavy rain moved through. A wind gust of 52 mph was recorded at the Missoula International Airport, with the main core of the storm passing to the east of the airport.
A 40 x 60 metal shed destroyed from collapsing thunderstorm wind gusts. Nearby observations recorded wind gusts in excess of 70 mph.
